title: Feature/1962
summary: In a shared session, each person's place in the chapter is shown as a colored bar (a **viewing area**) in the margin beside the verses. With many people this gets crowded, so the host now has a **Viewing areas** setting: show everyone's bars, only the hosts' bars, or **Automatic** (everyone when fewer than 4 people are in the session, only hosts at 4 or more). Each person can also override this for their own screen in **Settings**.

links.label: Issue 1962: Add a shared session setting to only show indicators for hosts

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use a laptop or desktop with Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari. Open the preview link above. If it shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload. If the page still looks like the old Seed Bible, do a hard refresh (**Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac).

setup.title: Get four browser windows ready
setup.body: You'll play up to four people, so you need four windows that don't share a sign-in. For example: a normal Chrome window (the **host**), a Chrome incognito window (**Ctrl+Shift+N**, or **Cmd+Shift+N** on Mac), a normal Firefox window, and a Firefox private window (**Ctrl+Shift+P**, or **Cmd+Shift+P** on Mac). A second computer or a phone works too. The host must be signed in (Seed Bible emails you a code, so use an inbox you can check). The other three people (**Guest A**, **Guest B**, **Guest C**) can stay signed out unless a test says otherwise.

setup.title: Start a shared session with one guest
setup.body: As the host, open **John 3**, click **Share**, then **Start and share session**. A link is copied to your clipboard. Open it in **Guest A**'s window only for now (hard refresh there once if the page looks old). Don't open it in the other windows yet.

setup.title: What a viewing area looks like
setup.body: When someone else in the session is reading the same chapter, a thin colored bar appears in the margin beside the verses they have on their screen, with their small round avatar at the top of it. You never see a bar for yourself. To make bars easy to tell apart, have each guest scroll so a different part of John 3 is on their screen (for example Guest A near verse 1, Guest B near verse 16, Guest C near verse 30).

tests.title: Session settings has a new Viewing areas choice, set to Automatic
steps: As the host, click the avatar row beside the reader's tool buttons and choose **Session settings**.
Find the **Viewing areas** section.
expected: There are three buttons: **Automatic**, **Everyone**, **Hosts only**.
**Automatic** is selected.
The text under them reads: `Show everyone's place when fewer than 4 people are here, and only hosts when there are 4 or more.`

tests.title: Only the host can change Viewing areas
steps: In Guest A's window, open the avatar row beside the reader's tools and look for **Session settings**. If Guest A can reach the Session settings window at all, find **Viewing areas** and try clicking **Hosts only**.
expected: Guest A has no **Session settings** entry, or if they reach it, the Viewing areas buttons are grayed out and clicking does nothing.

tests.title: The description changes with the choice
steps: As the host, in Session settings, click **Everyone**, then **Hosts only**, then **Automatic** again, reading the text under the buttons each time.
expected: Everyone: `Show where everyone is reading.`
Hosts only: `Show where the hosts are reading.`
Automatic: the 'fewer than 4 people' text from before.
The clicked button looks selected each time.

sections.title: Automatic: everyone below 4 people, hosts only at 4 or more
sections.intro: Leave Viewing areas on **Automatic** for this section. Everyone should stay on John 3.

tests.title: With 2 or 3 people, everyone's bars show
steps: With just the host and Guest A in the session, look at the margin beside the verses in each window.
Open the session link in **Guest B**'s window and scroll it to around verse 16. Wait a few seconds.
Look at the margin in all three windows.
expected: With 2 people: the host sees Guest A's bar, and Guest A sees the host's bar.
With 3 people: each window shows a bar for each of the other two people (for example Guest A sees both the host's and Guest B's bars).

tests.title: When a 4th person joins, only the host's bar shows
tests.why: This is the default the issue asks for: hosts only once there are 4 or more people.
steps: Open the session link in **Guest C**'s window and scroll it to around verse 30. Wait a few seconds.
Look at the margin in all four windows.
expected: Each guest's window shows **only the host's** bar; the other guests' bars are gone.
The host's window shows **no** bars, since nobody else is a host.

tests.title: When someone leaves and it drops to 3 people, everyone's bars come back
steps: Close **Guest C**'s window (or tab). Wait several seconds.
Look at the margin in the remaining three windows.
expected: The guests' bars reappear: each window again shows a bar for each of the other two people.

sections.title: Host picks Everyone or Hosts only

setup.title: Have 4 people in the session
setup.body: Reopen the session link in Guest C's window so the host and Guests A, B and C are all in the session on John 3, each scrolled to a different part of the chapter.

tests.title: Everyone shows all bars even with 4 people
steps: As the host, open **Session settings** and click **Everyone** under Viewing areas.
Look at the margin in all four windows.
expected: Within a few seconds, every window shows a bar for each of the other three people, without anyone reloading.

tests.title: Hosts only hides guests' bars even with 2 people
steps: Close Guest B's and Guest C's windows so only the host and Guest A are left. Wait a few seconds.
As the host, in Session settings, click **Hosts only**.
Look at both windows.
expected: Guest A still sees the host's bar.
The host no longer sees Guest A's bar.

tests.title: A co-host's bar shows under Hosts only
tests.why: Co-hosts count as hosts for this setting.
tests.before: Viewing areas is still on **Hosts only**. Reopen the session link in Guest B's window so there are 3 people. Making someone a co-host may require them to be signed in; if **Make co-host** isn't offered for Guest A, sign Guest A in with a different email than the host and try again.
steps: Check the host's window: Guest A's bar should not be showing.
As the host, in Session settings, under **Participants**, choose **Make co-host** for Guest A.
Look at the host's and Guest B's windows.
expected: The host now sees Guest A's bar.
Guest B sees both the host's and Guest A's bars, but not any bar for themselves.

sections.title: Each person's own override in Settings

setup.title: Reset the session
setup.body: As the host, set Viewing areas back to **Automatic**, and in Participants turn Guest A's co-host off again if it's on. Have the host and Guests A, B and C all in the session (4 people), so by default each guest sees only the host's bar.

tests.title: Settings has a Viewing areas dropdown under Session
steps: In Guest A's window, open **Settings**, then **Display & Theme**.
Scroll to the **Session** heading.
expected: Below **Verse Selection Effects** there is a **Viewing areas** dropdown set to **Default**, with the options **Default**, **Everyone** and **Hosts only**.
Under it, a description starts `Default follows the session: everyone's place when fewer than 4 people are here, and only hosts at 4 or more`.

tests.title: Picking Everyone shows all bars for that person only
steps: In Guest A's Settings, set **Viewing areas** to **Everyone**, then go back to the John 3 session.
Look at the margin in Guest A's and Guest B's windows.
expected: Guest A sees bars for the host, Guest B and Guest C.
Guest B still sees only the host's bar; Guest A's choice didn't change anyone else's screen.

tests.title: Picking Hosts only overrides the host's Everyone
steps: As the host, set the session's Viewing areas to **Everyone**.
In Guest B's window, open **Settings** → **Display & Theme** and set **Viewing areas** to **Hosts only**, then go back to the session.
Look at Guest B's and Guest C's windows.
expected: Guest B sees only the host's bar.
Guest C, still on Default, sees everyone's bars, following the host's Everyone choice.

tests.title: Setting it back to Default follows the session again
steps: In Guest A's and Guest B's Settings, set **Viewing areas** back to **Default**.
As the host, set the session back to **Automatic**.
Look at the guests' windows.
expected: With 4 people on Automatic, every guest is back to seeing only the host's bar.

tests.title: A signed-in person's choice is remembered after a reload
tests.before: This needs a guest who is signed in with a different email than the host. Sign Guest A in if they aren't already.
steps: In Guest A's Settings, set **Viewing areas** to **Hosts only**.
Reload Guest A's page, then open **Settings** → **Display & Theme** again.
expected: **Viewing areas** still shows **Hosts only**.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Other session settings still work
steps: As the host, in Session settings, change **Verse Selection Effects** to **Everyone**, then back to **Hosts only**.
Turn **Only host can navigate** on, then off again.
expected: Each change takes effect as before, and the **Viewing areas** choice doesn't change when you change these.

tests.title: Avatars in the sidebar and Participants list still show everyone
tests.why: The new setting only hides the bars in the margin, not who is in the session.
steps: With 4 people on Automatic (guests see only the host's bar), open the Participants pop-up from the avatar row in a guest's window.
expected: All four people are still listed, and the avatar row beside the reader's tools still shows everyone.

notCovered: Older shared sessions started before this change: the code treats them as Automatic, but testing that needs a session created on the old version.
Importing a settings file exported before this change (the new option defaults to Default); covered by unit tests.
Resetting all settings back to defaults also resets Viewing areas to Default; not reached through a single obvious button.
